1.  Present claim petition has been filed under Section 166 and 140 of M.V. Act seeking compensation in respect of injuries suffered by petitioner Upender Pandey in an accident taken place on 29/30.12.2015. It is stated that on 29.12.2015 petitioner was going to his home and on his way at Metro Site, U.P. Border, Mata Mandir, G.T. Road some persons were standing near fire. The petitioner stood there and after some time at about 3 a.m. a Man Lift crane make 10 Ton capacity,
model Genie Z45, Machine serial no:Z4508-1320 (hereinafter referred as offending vehicle), which was engaged in metro work came from behind and hit the petitioner due to which petitioner suffered grievous injuries. Petitioner was taken to Yashoda Hospital by the driver of the crane and an employee of metro. Regarding the accident in question an FIR No.98/2016 was registered in PS Sahibabad under Section 279/338 IPC. It is stated that at the time of accident petitioner was 35 years old and was earning Rs.15,000/- to Rs.20,000/- per month while working as a helper in a transport company. 
2. Originally claim petition was filed against four respondents. Respondent no.1 being DMRC at whose site the accident had occurred. It is stated that respondent no.2 is owner of offending crane belonging to Man Lift India Private Limited and respondent no.3 is driver of the same. Offending vehicle is stated to be insured with respondent no.4/insurance company (HDFC Ergo General Insurance).
3. During the pendency of claim petition an application under Order 1 Rule 10 CPC was moved on behalf of respondent no.1 to implead M/s GYT-TPL JV as the civil work of metro project at the DMRC site of MACT No.1710/2016 by SHAILENDER Page 2 SHAILENDER MALIK MALIK Date:
2024.05.17 16:47:07 +0530 Dilshad Garden to New Bus Adda Ghaziabad was awarded to M/s GYT- TPL JV, under an agreement. Said application was allowed vide order dated 14.12.2017 and M/s GYT-TPL JV was impleaded as respondent no.5.
4. Initially respondent no.4/insurance failed to file the WS despite giving opportunities,
consequently defence was closed vide order dated 06.02.2018. Thereafter an application was moved on behalf of respondent no.4/insurance seeking permission to file WS on record. Said application was allowed vide order dated 28.09.2018 and WS of respondent no.4 was taken on record. 
5. WS on behalf respondent no.1/Delhi Metro Rail Corporation Limited has been filed wherein an objection has been taken that there is no cause of action against R1 as the R1 had already awarded the contract C-87 for civil works from Dilshad Garden to New Bus Adda, Ghaziabad to M/s GYT-TPL JV (respondent no.5) and safety and security at the working site was sole responsibility of R5. Contents of claim petition have been denied in totality. 
6. WS on behalf respondent no.2 and 3 has been filed wherein it is pleaded that injured himself went to the site of construction and stood there. It is admitted that injured was taken to hospital by crane driver and staff of Metro. It is denied that accident took place due to rash and negligent driving of respondent no.3. It is pleaded that petitioner was standing without any cogent reason nor he was employee of respondents. Contents of claim petition as well as liability to pay compensation have been denied.

2 7. In its WS respondent no.4/insurance company has taken the objection that no cause of action arose under M.V. Act against the offending crane/machine. It is pleaded that R4 is insurer of contractor's MACT No.1710/2016 SHAILENDER MALIK Page 3 MALIK Date: 2024.05.17 16:47:16 +0530 plant and machinery under the Contractor's Plant and Machinery Policy no.2224200502506602000 valid from 09.10.2015 to 15.05.2016 but the same is not applicable to provisions of M.V. Act. It is pleaded that as per Section 8 of the policy as R4 never issued any policy under the provision of Section 146 of M.V. Act and as such does not provide coverage of third party risks on public road. Contents of claim petition have been denied. 
8. Respondent no.5 in its WS has taken the objection that R5 has been impleaded at a belated stage but being the contractor for Metro site where the alleged accident took place. It is stated that no cause of action arose against R5. It is pleaded that there is no contributory negligence on the part of R5 and it is petitioner himself who without any authority or right intruded into and remained at the cordoned off area at construction site at odd hours. It is pleaded that in view of Work Order dated 11.12.2015 respondent no.5 is not liable to pay any compensation to petitioner as the contractor/R2 is liable for liability arising out of site activities carried out by it. Contents of claim petition have been denied. 
9. On the basis of pleadings of parties following issues were framed by ld. Predecessor on 06.02.2018 : 
(1)Whether petitioner suffered injuries during the accident occurred on 30.12.2015 at 3.00 am at Metro Site, UP Border, near Mata Mandir, GT Road, Sahibabad, due to rash and negligent driving of the vehicle/Machine Serial No.Z4508-1320 being driven by respondent no.3/driver? OPP (2)Whether petitioner is entitled for compensation, if so, to what extend and from whom? OPP (3)Relief. 
10. Petitioner in order to substantiate his claim examined three witnesses. PW1 is Yogender Pandey,
brother of the petitioner/injured, PW2 MACT No.1710/2016 by SHAILENDER Page 4 SHAILENDER MALIK MALIK Date: 2024.05.17 16:47:23 +0530 is petitioner Upender Pandey himself and PW3 is Dr.Sushil Kamal who proved disability certificate of petitioner. 
11. On behalf of respondent no.1/Delhi Metro Rail Corporation Limited one witness R1W1 Piyush Goyla, Junior Engineer/Civil has been examined. Respondent no.4 examined one witness R4W1 Simarpreet Kaur, Deputy Manager (Litigation and Claims) of insurance company. On behalf of respondent no.5 one witness R5W1 Rajesh Kumar Singh, Manager Human Resources has been examined. 
12. I have heard Sh.Vivek Bhati, ld. Counsel for petitioner, Sh.Ajay Kumar, ld. counsel for R2 & R3,
Sh.Shrey Mehta, ld. Counsel for R4/insurance company as well as Sh.Yashvir Kumar, ld. Counsel for R5. I have also gone through written submissions filed on behalf of petitioner. Issue No.1 13. It is settled proposition of law that an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non. However, the standard of Upender Pandey vs Delhi Metro Corporation Ltd on 17 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122640175/
3 proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities. Holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the Claim Petition based upon negligence. Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal. Reference may be made to the judgments titled as New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v.
Sakshi Bhutani & Others. (MAC APP. No. 550/2011 decided on 02.07.2012), Bimla Devi & Others v. 
Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Others (2009) 13 SC 530, Parmeshwari v. Amirchand &
Others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 & Mangla Ram v. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. & Others 2018 Law Suit (SC) 303. 
14 . For proving the rash and negligent driving of offending MACT No.1710/2016 SHAILENDER Page 5 SHAILENDER MALIK MALIK Date: 2024.05.17 16:47:31 +0530 vehicle PW2 petitioner/injured has deposed that on 29.12.2015 he was proceeding towards his house, while on the way at Metro site of UP Border, Mata Mandir Marg, GT Road some persons were standing as there was some fire at that place. PW2 says that he stood there for some time. At about 3.00 a.m. 
PW2 says that a Man Lift Crane, engaged in Metro work came from behind and hit him, due to which he fell down and suffered grievous injuries. PW2 says that driver of the crane and other employee of Metro toom him to Yashoda Hospital, Kaushambi. PW2 also referred to the registration of FIR No.0098/2016 at PS Sahibabad UP on 19.01.2016 u/s 279/338 IPC.
15. Nothing substantive came int eh cross examination of PW2 rather witness reiterated in hhis cross examination that whiile he saw some persons standing near hte fire, he stood for the time being and in the meantime the crane hit him from behind. PW2 in cross examination by counsel for insurance specifically denied the suggestion of accident having taken place due to his negligence or carelessness. As such nothing came in the cross examination of PW2 to disbelieve the version regrding the accident as well as the factum of rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle/crane which hit the petitioner from behind. Evidence of PW2 gets corroboration from the factum of criminal case registered against respondent no.3/driver of the offending vehicle. In the evidence of PW2 copy of FIR, complaint given to SHO PS Sahibabad as well as certified copy of report u/s 173 Cr.PC has been proved showing that it is respondent no.3/driver who has been prosecuted in criminal case for the accident in question. As such it is clearly established that petitioner/injured suffered injuries due to rash and negligent driving of driver/respondent no.3 while driving offending vehicle/crane. Issue accordingly decided in favour of MACT No.1710/2016 by SHAILENDER SHAILENDER MALIK Page 6 MALIK Date: 2024.05.17 16:47:40 +0530 petitioner and against the respondents. 
Issue No.2 16. The scope of compensation in injury cases has been considered by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case titled as Mr. R.D. Hattangadi v. M/s Pest Control (India) Pvt. Ltd., 1995 AIR 755. The relevant extract is as under:
"Broadly speaking while fixing an amount of compensation payable to a victim of an accident, the damages have to be assessed separately as pecuniary damages and special damages. Pecuniary damages are those which the victim has actually incurred Upender Pandey vs Delhi Metro Corporation Ltd on 17 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122640175/
4 and which is capable of being calculated in terms of money-, whereas non-pecuniary damages are those which are incapable of being assessed by arithmetical calculations. 
In order to appreciate two concepts pecuniary damages may, include expenses incurred by the claimant: (i) medical attendance; (ii) loss of earning of profit upto the date of trial; (iii) other material loss. So far non- pecuniary damages are concerned ,
they may include (i) damages for mental and physical shock, pain suffering, already suffered or likely to be suffered in future; (ii) damages to compensate for the loss of amenities of life which may include a variety of matters i.e. on account of injury the claimant may not be able to walk, run or sit;
(iii) damages for the loss of expectation of life, i.e. on account of injury the normal longevity of the person concerned is shortened; (iv) inconvenience, discomfort,
disappointment, hardship, frustration and mental stress in life." 
17. Further, in Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar & another (2011) 1 SCC 343, Hon'ble Supreme Court of India laid down general principles for computation of compensation in injury cases. The relevant paras of the judgment are reproduced as under:
4. The provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, MACT No.1710/2016 by SHAILENDER SHAILENDER MALIK Page 7 MALIK Date: 2024.05.17 16:47:52 +0530 1988 ("the Act", for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident. The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner. The court or the Tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy,
though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable. A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury. This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned. 
5. The heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following:
Pecuniary Damages (special damages) 
(i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation,
nourishing food and miscellaneous expenditure.
(ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising:
Upender Pandey vs Delhi Metro Corporation Ltd on 17 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122640175/
5 (a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment.
(b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability.
(iii) Future medical expenses.
Non-Pecuniary Damages (general damages)
(iv) Damages to pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries.
(v) Loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage)
(vi) Loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal longevity).
MACT No.1710/2016 Digitally signed by Page 8 SHAILENDER SHAILENDER MALIK MALIK Date:
2024.05.17 16:47:58 +0530 In routine personal injury cases, compensation will be awarded only under heads (i), (ii), (a) and (iv). It is only in serious cases of injury, where there is specific medical evidence corroborating the evidence of the claimant, that compensation will be granted under any of the heads (ii), (b), (iii), (v) and (vi) relating to loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability, future medical expenses, loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage) and loss of expectation of life.
18. In the light of the aforementioned judgments, the compensation to which the petitioner is entitled shall be as under:-
PECUNIARY DAMAGES :
Medical Expenses:
19. PW2/petitioner in his evidence has deposed that he incurred huge amount on his treatment i.e.
Rs.50,000/- on medicines. To prove this fact petitioner has proved medical bills as Ex.PW2/2 (colly.) totaling of which comes out to be Rs.9,273/-. There is no cross-examination of petitioner on these medical bills. As such petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.9,273/- as medical expenses. 
Loss of earning during treatment:
20. Petitioner (PW2) in his deposition stated that at the time of accident he was working as a helper in a transport company and was earning Rs.15,000/- to Rs.20,000/- per month from the said job. 
PW2 also states that he used to give about Rs.10,000/- to Rs.15,000/- per month to his parents to meet out household expenses. PW2 however in his cross examination stated that he is engaged as a labourer on daily wages but he has no fixed employer. PW2 stated that his daily earning was between Rs.500-Rs.700 per day and his monthly income was approximately Rs.18,000/- to Rs.20,000/-. During cross examination by counsel for MACT No.1710/2016 by SHAILENDER Upender Pandey vs Delhi Metro Corporation Ltd on 17 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122640175/
6 SHAILENDER MALIK Page 9 MALIK Date: 2024.05.17 16:48:06 +0530 insurance PW2 stated that he has not filed any document to show that he is employed and that he is working. He also stated that he has not filed anything on record to show that he suffered financial losses. 
21. Taking into consideration the evidence of PW2 on the face of it, in the absence of any documentary evidence regarding his earning of Rs.15,000/- to Rs.20,000/- as claimed, income of petitioner would be taken at parity with minimum wages of unskilled worker at the time of accident in Delhi i.e. Rs.9,178/- per month. 
22. It has further come in the evidence of PW2 that petitioner suffered multiple grievous injuries and remained admitted in Yashoda Hospital from 29.12.2015 to 05.01.2016. It has also come in the evidence that petitioner suffered 57% of permanent disability in relation to right lower limb as per disability certificate Ex.PW2/6.
23. Thus taking into consideration the medical problems faced by the petitioner, medical documents also indicate that various procedures were done during treatment of the petitioner, as such petitioner must have remained confined to bed for 03 months. As such petitioner is entitled for loss of earning due to accidental injuries for sum of Rs.27,534/- (Rs.9,178 X 03 months).
Loss of future earning due to disability :
24. In case of Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011) 1 SCC 343, Hon'ble Supreme Court of India determined the broad criteria for assessment of permanent disability for ascertaining the purpose of future loss of earning and also laid down step by step procedure for assessment of disability and for ascertainment to the effect of the permanent disability on the actual earning capacity. Relevant paras of the judgment are reproduced as under:-
MACT No.1710/2016 SHAILENDER  Page 10  MALIK Date: 2024.05.17  16:48:13 +0530 "9. Therefore, the Tribunal has to first decide whether there is any permanent disability and if so,
the extent of such permanent disability. This means that the tribunal should consider and decide with reference to the evidence:
(i) Whether the disablement is permanent or temporary;
(ii) If the disablement is permanent, whether it is permanent total disablement or permanent partial disablement;
(iii) If the disablement percentage is expressed with reference to any specific limb,
then the effect of such disablement of the limb on the functioning of the entire body,
Upender Pandey vs Delhi Metro Corporation Ltd on 17 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122640175/
7 that is the permanent disability suffered by the person. 
If the Tribunal concludes that there is no permanent disability then there is no question of proceeding further and determining the loss of future earning capacity. But if the Tribunal concludes that there is permanent disability then it will proceed to ascertain its extent. After the Tribunal ascertains the actual extent of permanent disability of the claimant based on the medical evidence, it has to determine whether such permanent disability has affected or will affect his earning capacity. 
10. Ascertainment of the effect of the permanent disability on the actual earning capacity involves three steps. The tribunal has to first ascertain what activities of the claimant could carry on in spite of the permanent disability and what he could not do as a result of permanent disability (this is also relevant for awarding compensation under the head of loss of amenities of life). The second step is to ascertain his avocation, profession and nature of work before the accident, as also his age. The third step is to find out whether (i) the claimant is totally disabled from earning any kind of livelihood or (ii) whether in spite of the permanent disability, the claimant could still effectively carry on the activities and functions, which he was earlier carrying on, or (iii) Whether he was prevented or restricted from discharging his previous MACT No.1710/2016 by SHAILENDER Page 11 SHAILENDER MALIK MALIK Date: 2024.05.17 16:48:19 +0530 activities and functions so that he continues to earn or can continue to earn his livelihood."
....If doctor has given evidence about percentage of permanent disability, Tribunal will have to seek doctors opinion as to whether it is possible to deduce the corresponding functional permanent disability with reference to whole body and if so to what percentage.
13. We may now summarize the principles discussed above:
(i). All injuries (or permanent disabilities arising from injuries), do not result in loss of earning capacity. 
(ii). The percentage of permanent disability with reference to the whole body of a person, cannot be assumed to be the percentage of loss of earning capacity. To put it differently, the percentage of loss of earning capacity is not the same as the percentage of permanent disability (except in a few cases, where the Tribunal on the basis of evidence, concludes that percentage of loss of earning capacity is the same as percentage of permanent disability). 
(iii). The doctor who treated an injured- claimant or who examined him subsequently to assess the extent of his permanent disability can give evidence only in regard the extent of permanent disability. The loss of earning capacity is something that will have to be assessed by the Tribunal with reference to the evidence in entirety. 
(iv). The same permanent disability may result in different percentages of loss of earning capacity in different persons, depending upon the nature of profession,
Upender Pandey vs Delhi Metro Corporation Ltd on 17 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122640175/
8 occupation or job, age, education and other factors."
25. Keeping in view the ratio as discussed above, in the present MACT No.1710/2016 by SHAILENDER Page 12 SHAILENDER MALIK MALIK Date: 2024.05.17 16:48:26 +0530 case it is evident on record that as a result of the injuries sustained by petitioner in an accident, he suffered 57% permanent disability in relation to right lower limb. In this regard PW3 Dr.Sushil Kamal,
Senior Resident, Orthopedic Department, GTB Hospital, Delhi, produced the record relating to disability certificate no.709/09/07/18 dated 02.07.2018, issued to injured Upender Pandey which is Ex.PW2/6. The disablement and loss of earning capacity are two different aspects and may not corresponding to each other and the loss of income has to be seen considering the profession in which the petitioner was engaged at the time of accident. As per case of petitioner, he was working as a helper/labourer at the time of accident. 
26. It is argued by the counsel for the petitioner that due to accidental injuries and permanent disability, petitioner lost his livelihood as he is unable to do his work properly. Dr.Sushil Kamal (PW3) who proved medical disability certificate of petitioner/injured during cross examination has stated that petitioner will not be able to sit cross legged, squat or kneel down. He also stated that petitioner will face difficulty in walking on uneven surfaces and surfaces which bear a slope as well as difficulty in climbing stairs and to lift weight. 
27. In Raj Kumar vs. Ajay Kumar (supra) Hon'ble Apex Court in para 11 and 12 has observed that Tribunal should not be a silent spectator when medical evidence is tendered regarding injuries. 
Tribunal is required to hold inquiry into the claim for determining just compensation by assessing the medical permanent disability as well as functional disability keeping in view nature of work,
profession etc. of the injured. The percentage of permanent disability of whole body cannot be presumed to be percentage loss of earning. Therefore Tribunal is bound to assess corresponding functional disability to compute the future loss of income. 
MACT No.1710/2016 SHAILENDER Page 13  SHAILENDER MALIK  MALIK Date: 2024.05.17  16:48:34 +0530 28. Having considered the entire evidence, medical documents reflect that petitioner suffered grievous injuries and suffered 57% of permanent disability. However when this Tribunal has to assess the functional disability vis a vis medical disability, certain factors like nature of job, nature of injury, age, future avenues etc. are to be seen. In the present case no evidence has been led about the exact nature of job except a bald assertion that petitioner was working as helper/labour. Even if we take such assertion on the face of it, in this case medical disability of 57% is in relation to right lower limb, therefore in such circumstances when petitioner has lost his livelihood as he used to work as a labourer/helper on account of his accidental injuries, this Tribunal is of considered view that the functional disability of the petitioner in relation to his job is taken to be 28.5%. For assessing the future prospects, petitioner would considered to be suffering from functional disability to the extent of 28.5%. 
Upender Pandey vs Delhi Metro Corporation Ltd on 17 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122640175/
9 29. Further, law is well settled that there should be no departure from the multiplier method in injury cases also [refer: Sandeep Khanuja vs. Atul Dande & Anr., (2017) 3 SCC 351]. As per photocopy of Aadhar card of petitioner/injured Ex.PW1/1, date of birth of petitioner is 10.02.1979. 
As such age of petitioner as on date of accident i.e. 29.12.2015 was 36 years. As such multiplier to be applied in the present case would be 15 as applicable to age group between 36-40 years, would be applicable as per settled principle laid down in case of Sarla Verma v. DTC (2009) 6 SCC 121. 
Moreover, the law has been well settled by the decisions of Supreme Court in the cases of Sandeep Khanuja (supra) and Erudhaya Priya vs. State Express Transport Corporation Ltd., 2020 SCC OnLine SC 601, that while applying the multiplier method, future prospects on advancement in life and career are also to be taken into consideration. 
MACT No.1710/2016 SHAILENDER Page 14  SHAILENDER MALIK  MALIK Date: 2024.05.17  16:48:41 +0530 Thus, considering the petitioner was being not having any permanent job and below the age of 40 years at the time of accident, an addition of income to the extent of 40% towards future prospects has to be counted. 
30. As discussed above, the income of petitioner has been assessed Rs.9,178/- + 40% (Rs.3,671/-),
total Rs.12,849/-. Thus applying the functional disability to be 28.5% of Rs.12,849/-, amount comes out to be Rs.3,662/-. As such the loss of future income due to disability comes out to be Rs.3,662 X 12 X 15 = Rs.6,59,160/-. 
Special Diet & Conveyance Charges:
31. Petitioner (PW2) in his deposition stated that due to accidental injuries he has spent Rs.40,000/- on special diet and Rs.30,000/- on conveyance charges. Since it has come on record that petitioner suffered grievous injuries on different parts of his body and as per medical documents, this Tribunal awarded compensation under the head of loss of earning during treatment for a period of three months. It has also come in the evidence of petitioner that he remained admitted in Yashoda Hospital Kaushambi from 29.12.2015 to 05.01.2016. Therefore this Tribunal is of the considered opinion that petitioner must have incurred expenses towards special diet for his well being during the period of treatment and also incurred expenses towards going to different hospitals. Thus this Tribunal awards compensation of Rs.20,000/- under the head of special diet and Rs.20,000/- under the head of conveyance charges to the petitioner. Attendant Charges:
32. Petitioner in his evidence has claimed that he spent Rs.60,000/- towards engaging an attendant for his well being. Since this Tribunal has already assessed compensation to the petitioner for a period of three months under the head of loss of earning during treatment. Though MACT No.1710/2016 SHAILENDER MALIK Date: 2024.05.17 16:48:48 +0530 no documentary evidence in this regard has been led by the petitioner, but fact remains that he suffered grievous injuries on different parts of his body and as per disability certificate his medical disability has been found to be 57% and same has been assessed by this Tribunal in relation to his functional disability to be 28.5% . 
Upender Pandey vs Delhi Metro Corporation Ltd on 17 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122640175/
10 Keeping in view the medical documents placed on record, this Tribunal is of the view that petitioner must have engaged the services of some attendant and he is required to be awarded compensation under this head for a period of three months. Therefore petitioner in the opinion of this Tribunal is also entitled for attendant charges at parity with minimum wages of unskilled worker at the time of accident in Delhi i.e. Rs.9,178/- per month. As such petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.27,534/- (Rs.9,178 X 03 months). NON PECUNIARY DAMAGES :
Pain & Sufferings:
33. While discussing the criteria to ascertain the compensation for pain and sufferings by victim of vehicular accident, observations of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in Satya Narain v. Jai Kishan, FAO No:
709/02, date of decision: 02.02.2007 can be considered: 
"12. On account of pain and suffering, suffice would it be to note that it is difficult to measure pain and suffering in terms of a money value. However, compensation which has to be paid must bear some objectives co-relation with the pain and suffering. 
13. The objective facts relatable to pain and suffering would be:
(a) Nature of injury.
(b) Body part affected (c) Duration of the treatment."
34. In this case, as per MLC of petitioner which is Ex.PW2/4 he was found to have suffered grievous injuries on his right thigh, right ankle MACT No.1710/2016 by SHAILENDER SHAILENDER MALIK Page 16 MALIK Date: 2024.05.17 16:48:54 +0530 and other parts of body. The treatment record and bills/invoices of pharmacy further show that petitioner had been taking continuous treatment. Thus, it is clear that petitioner must have suffered immense pain and suffering during his treatment and therefore, I am of the opinion that an amount of Rs.1,00,000/- would be just and fair compensation for pain, sufferings and mental trauma suffered by the petitioner as consequences of injuries sustained in the accident. Accordingly, Rs.1,00,000/- is granted to the petitioner under this head. 
Loss of Amenities:
35. It is evident on record that even after completion of treatment, petitioner sustained 57% medical permanent physical disability in relation to right lower limb which has been assessed as 28.5%
functional disability in relation to whole body of the petitioner by this Tribunal. It cannot be ignored that with the aforementioned disability, petitioner is bound to face difficulties throughout his life Upender Pandey vs Delhi Metro Corporation Ltd on 17 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122640175/
11 and will not be able to enjoy the amenities of life to the fullest. In view of this, the petitioner is granted a compensation of Rs.50,000/- under this head. 
Loss of Marriage Prospects 36. In this case on behalf of petitioner claim has also been made for compensation on account of loss of marriage prospects. PW2 Upender Pandey in his evidence has stated that he unmarried. One cannot ignore the aspect that on account of accidental injuries and consequential permanent disability suffered by the petitioner, his marriage avenues must have been adversely affected. 
Therefore this Tribunal finds that though no exact quantification of loss of marriage prospect can be determined. However a lump sum amount of Rs.1,00,000/- is ordered to be awarded under the above said head. 
MACT No.1710/2016 by SHAILENDER Page 17  SHAILENDER MALIK  MALIK Date: 2024.05.17  16:49:01 +0530 37. Thus, the compensation awarded to the petitioner is summarized as under:-
